_comment: The one place the pipeline's sources are declared. `npm run refresh` and
the scheduled job both read this file, so a URL that moves is fixed here
and nowhere else. Keys are refresh-curve.mjs's own option names (the CLI's
--json-path is jsonPath here); order matters, because a later source wins
Makam is listed LAST so it owns the 1y overlap, where it reads ~3.28%
against shcd08's ~3.21%. Reversing the order silently changes the 1y point
and the whole short end's attribution.
TASE's securities table, filtered to T-Bills (cl1 6 is the T-Bills
group from security/securitiesclassifications; lang 2 and pageNum are
both required — omit either and the response is an empty list rather
than an error). Accept-Language is what the WAF actually checks:
without it the endpoint answers 403 to an otherwise identical request.
Yield and day count both come from TASE rather than being derived: the
two were computed there at the same instant, so they agree with each
other. Deriving the tenor from RedemptionDate instead means guessing
which day TASE measured from, and at the front of the curve one day of
If the WAF refuses the runner, the committed snapshot is used instead.
